logline: The demon lord Satan, stripped of his magic and stranded in modern Tokyo, has no choice but to survive by flipping burgers at a fast-food joint while his nemesis hero hunts him down.

renewal.note: Two seasons aired between 2013 and 2023. No further seasons have been announced as of 2026, and the source light novel series concluded.

bollymeter.basis: Season 1 holds a 7.79 MyAnimeList score from hundreds of thousands of ratings. Reviewers praised its nimble genre-flipping - fantasy fish-out-of-water comedy executed with lively animation and sharp comic timing.

pull_quotes.text: It's funny when it needs to be, cool when it needs to be, and feel-good when it needs to be.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 of Hataraku Maou-sama landed in Spring 2013 as a tightly produced 13-episode comedy that pulled off a genuinely clever premise: a world-conquering demon lord humbled by the grind of minimum-wage Tokyo life. White Fox animated the culture-shock gags with a light touch, and the ensemble - Satan as an earnest part-timer, the hero Emi Yusa as his grudge-holding neighbor - generated genuine chemistry. Critics awarded it solid marks for execution, noting the comedy worked best in the first half before the novelty wore thin. A 7.79 MyAnimeList score reflects a strong consensus that Season 1 delivers a satisfying genre lark even if its story never builds to a definitive conclusion.

episode_reviews.title: The Devil Arrives in Sasazuka
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere earns its premise in a single act - a world-ending battle collapses into an argument about train fares - and the tonal whiplash is exactly the joke the whole series is built on.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Satan mispronouncing the station name while clutching a grocery bag is the moment that crystallises why the concept works.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 returned after a nine-year gap to mixed reception. Reviewers found the expanded plot threads vague and the comedy less effective once the novelty of the premise had fully dissolved.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived in Summer 2022, nine years after the original run, produced by a new studio (3Hz) under Disney+ streaming rights for its second part. The delay proved costly: the novelty engine that powered Season 1 had long since idled, and the new season's ambition to advance the actual fantasy plot landed as 'scattered, vague, and poorly structured' in the consensus of dedicated reviewers. Part 2 (2023) completed the adaptation of the light novels but left longtime fans divided. The series closed more as a completion exercise than a triumphant return.
seasons.season_over_season: Where Season 1 thrived on a contained comic premise executed with precision, Season 2 stretched into ambitious mythology that landed as vague and structurally loose.
